title: The Lost City
summary: Emily and Jack find a hidden city in the forest together slowly.
coverScene: Two hikers stand on a white stone bridge looking at a hidden city of gold towers nestled in a green valley.

sentences.text: Emily and Jack walked through the deep green forest during their long summer holiday trip.
The forest was high on the mountain side.
The air was cool and fresh, but the path was hard to find.
The thick trees made the way very dark.
Suddenly, Jack noticed a narrow opening between two massive rocks.
It seemed to lead toward a hidden valley below the peak.
They looked closely at the ground and found strange stone marks.
These marks were very old.
They pointed directly toward a place that was not on any modern map.
They decided to follow the trail.
They wondered what secret could be hidden in such a wild region.
As they moved deeper into the valley, the trees began to clear.
They saw a sight that was absolutely beautiful.
A whole city made of white stone and gold stood before them.
It shone brightly under the afternoon sun.
The buildings were unlike anything they had ever seen in history books.
The city had tall towers that reached the sky.
No noise came from the streets.
The entire place had been empty for many hundreds of years.
However, the gardens were full of colorful flowers.
This suggested that some force was still keeping the plants alive.
They felt wonder as they stepped onto the main street.
The street was covered with smooth stones of a silver color.
In the center of the city, they found a small temple.
Powerful ancient trees stood in a circle around it.
There was a stone table in front of the temple.
A small box was left open on the table.
It looked as if someone had just walked away.
Inside the box lay a map on a thin piece of metal.
Jack realized that the map was not just a guide.
It was a key that they needed to unlock the temple.
Thick clouds might cover the entrance later.
They studied the map and noticed several complex puzzles about the stars.
The first puzzle required them to move three large pieces of glass.
They had to make the light from the sun shine into the temple.
Emily was very good at solving difficult problems.
She used the map to calculate the correct angles.
The light hit the final glass and a loud sound moved through the square.
The heavy stone doors began to open.
They entered a large hall with pictures on the walls.
The pictures described the history of the ancient people.
These people had used a special kind of energy from the earth.
It was clear that the city was a place of great knowledge.
It was protected from the world by mystery and peace.
Deep inside the temple, they discovered a large room.
It was filled with a soft blue light from a large stone.
This stone was the source of power for the entire city.
However, the stone was currently becoming weak.
The walls began to shake.
According to the map, the city would only remain steady with a code.
They had to enter the code into the base machine.
Jack and Emily knew they had to act quickly.
The city was starting to disappear around them like a dream.
They would be trapped within a place that no longer existed.
The code used several marks that represented the elements of nature.
These marks were for water, fire, wind, and the earth.
Emily carefully pressed the marks in the correct order.
She followed a poem she had read on the wall.
For a moment, nothing happened.
The room was so silent that they could hear their own hearts.
Suddenly, the stone began to glow with a strong light.
The ground stopped moving as the energy returned.
The city was saved.
The blue light spread through the streets and the walls shone with life.
They felt a great sense of success.
They have preserved a piece of history that is truly unique.
They explored the rest of the temple.
They found a room with many books in a strange language.
Jack suggested that they should take one book back with them.
He wanted to show it to a professor at the university.
However, Emily felt that the city should remain a secret.
The presence of too many people might destroy it.
They realized that the city had chosen them to be its guards.
This role would require great responsibility.
If the world knows about this place, the government might take the energy.
They decided to leave the books where they were.
They only took the memory of their great adventure with them.
Before they left, the map began to change.
It showed a new path away from the city.
This path was much easier than the first one.
It led them back toward the main road.
They walked slowly through the city one last time.
They admired the great detail of the buildings and the peaceful gardens.
It was a place where time seemed to stand still.
They felt lucky to have experienced such an event.
They promised to return if the city called to them again.
The sun was beginning to set in the sky.
The clouds were red and orange as they reached the valley edge.
When they finally reached their car, the mountain was covered in thick clouds.
The hidden valley disappeared from their view.
They looked back, but there was no sign of the white towers.
The golden roofs they had seen before were gone.
Jack wondered if the city would still be there tomorrow.
Maybe it only appeared to those looking for adventure.
Emily smiled and held the small stone box as a sign.
It was the secret they now shared.
They drove home in silence and thought about the ancient people.
The experience had changed them both.
It gave them a new way to look at the world.

options: She wanted the gold for herself
She was afraid of the ancient people
She feared that many people would destroy it

sentences.text: Emily and Jack walked through the deep green forest that covered the high mountain side during their long summer holiday trip.
The air was cool and fresh, but the path they followed had become increasingly difficult to see among the thick trees.
Suddenly, Jack noticed a narrow opening between two massive rocks that appeared to lead toward a hidden valley below the peak.
If they had not been looking closely at the ground, they would have missed the strange stone marks on the floor.
These marks were very old, yet they seemed to point directly toward a place that was not on any modern map.
They decided to follow the trail, wondering what kind of secret could be hidden in such a remote and wild region.
As they moved deeper into the valley, the trees began to clear, revealing a sight that was absolutely beautiful and quite unexpected.
A whole city made of white stone and gold stood before them, and it shined brightly under the afternoon sun.
The architecture was unlike anything they had ever seen in history books, with tall towers that seemed to reach the sky.
No noise came from the streets, and it appeared as though the entire place had been empty for many hundreds of years.
However, the gardens were full of colorful flowers, which suggested that some force was still maintaining the life of this city.
They felt wonder as they stepped onto the main street, which was covered with smooth stones of a silver color.
In the center of the city, they found a small temple that was surrounded by a circle of ancient trees that looked powerful.
On a stone table in front of the temple, a small box was left open, as if someone had just walked away.
Inside the box lay a map that was drawn on a thin piece of metal, showing the plan of the city.
Jack realized that the map was not just a guide, but a key that would be necessary to unlock the temple.
If they had arrived a day later, the thick clouds might have covered the entrance, making it impossible to enter.
They studied the map carefully, noticing that it contained several complex puzzles that were related to the stars.
The first puzzle required them to move three large pieces of glass so that light from the sun would shine into the temple.
Emily, who was very good at solving difficult problems, managed to calculate the correct angles by using the map.
As the light hit the final glass, a loud sound moved through the square, and the heavy stone doors began to open.
They entered a large hall where the walls were covered with pictures that described the history of the people there.
These people had used a special kind of energy that was derived from the earth itself to build their wonderful home.
It was clear that the city was a place of great knowledge and peace, protected from the world by mystery.
Deep inside the temple, they discovered a large room that was filled with a soft, blue light from a large stone.
This stone was the source of power for the entire city, but it was currently becoming weak, causing the walls to shake.
According to the map, the city would only remain steady if a specific code was entered into the base machine.
Jack and Emily knew they had to act quickly because the city was starting to disappear around them like a dream.
If the energy failed, the city would be lost forever, and they would be trapped within a place that no longer existed.
They began to work together, using the information they had gathered from the ancient pictures to find the right code.
The code consisted of several symbols that represented the elements of nature, such as water, fire, wind, and the earth.
Emily carefully pressed the symbols in the order that was suggested by the poem she had read on the wall.
For a moment, nothing happened, and the silence in the room was so heavy they could hear the beat of their hearts.
Suddenly, the stone began to glow with an intense light, and the movement of the ground stopped as the energy returned.
The city was saved, and the blue light spread through the streets, making the white stone walls shine with life.
They felt a great sense of achievement, knowing that they had preserved a piece of history that was truly unique.
As they explored the rest of the temple, they found a room that contained many books written in a strange language.
Jack suggested that they should take one book back with them to show to a professor who studied ancient cultures.
However, Emily felt that the city should remain a secret, as the presence of too many people might destroy it.
They realized that they had been chosen by the city to be its guards, a role that would require responsibility.
If the world knew about this place, the government might try to take control of the energy for their own purposes.
They decided to leave the books where they were and only take the memory of their great adventure with them.
Before they left, they noticed that the map they had used was beginning to change, showing a new path away.
This path was much easier than the one they had taken to arrive, leading them back to the main road.
They walked slowly through the city one last time, admiring the great detail of the buildings and the peaceful gardens.
It was a place where time seemed to stand still, and they felt lucky to have experienced such an event.
They promised each other that they would return one day, but only if the city called to them again.
The sun was beginning to set, painting the sky with red and orange colors as they reached the valley edge.
When they finally reached their car, the mountain was covered in thick clouds, making the hidden valley disappear.
They looked back, but there was no sign of the white towers or the golden roofs they had seen before.
Jack wondered if the city would still be there tomorrow, or if it only appeared to those looking for adventure.
Emily smiled, holding the small stone box that she had kept as a sign of the secret they now shared.
They drove home in silence, each thinking about the mysterious city and the ancient people who had built it.
The experience had changed them both, giving them a new perspective on the mysteries that still exist in our world.

quiz.q: What did Emily and Jack find on the stone table in front of the temple?
options: A stone box with a map
A book about history
A piece of gold

quiz.q: What was causing the city walls to shake?
options: An earthquake in the mountains
The power source was becoming weak
The heavy stone doors were opening

quiz.q: Why did Emily think the city should remain a secret?
options: They wanted to keep the gold for themselves
To protect its beauty and avoid government control
Because they could not find the map again

sentences.text: Emily and Jack trudged through the deep green forest that clung to the high mountain side, their summer holiday stretching into an endless trek.
The air was cool and fresh, carrying the faint scent of pine and damp earth, while the narrow trail disappeared beneath tangled trunks.
Sunlight filtered through the canopy in thin shafts, painting the mossy floor with shifting gold, yet the path grew increasingly hard to discern.
Jack halted, his eyes narrowing as he spotted a narrow cleft between two massive rocks, a mouth-like opening that seemed to gape toward a hidden valley.
A sudden chill brushed their skin, and Emily felt an uncanny pull, as if the forest itself whispered that they were about to uncover something ancient.
On the ground, half-buried stone markings glimmered faintly, their weathered engravings forming a pattern that pointed toward a place absent from any modern map.
The symbols, though eroded, resembled constellations and geometric shapes, suggesting a guide left by hands long vanished.
Emily knelt, brushing away centuries of dust, and felt a faint vibration, as if the stones themselves were breathing.
Jack traced the line with his fingertip, noticing that it led deeper into the shadowed gorge, toward a darkness that promised both danger and wonder.
Without a word, they agreed to follow the trail, each step echoing a quiet pact to uncover the secret hidden in this remote wilderness.
The forest thinned gradually, and the oppressive canopy gave way to a sudden clearing that revealed a sight both breathtaking and impossible.
Before them rose a city of white stone and gold, its facades gleaming under the afternoon sun like a mirage of mythic proportions.
Towering spires stretched upward, their silhouettes slicing the sky, while silent streets lay empty, as though time itself had paused within the walls.
Yet gardens burst with color, roses and lilies swaying gently, hinting that an unseen hand still tended the blossoms, preserving life in a forgotten realm.
Emily felt her breath catch, a mixture of awe and trepidation, while Jack's pulse quickened, his mind racing with questions about the city's origins.
They stepped onto the main avenue, its surface smooth and silver-gray, reflecting the bright sky as if it were a river of light.
The air was filled with a faint hum, a melodic resonance that seemed to emanate from the stone itself, inviting them deeper.
At the heart of the city stood a modest temple, encircled by a ring of ancient trees whose trunks bore scars like old battle wounds.
In front of the altar lay an open wooden box, its lid tipped as if someone had just stepped away, revealing a thin metal sheet with a map.
The map was not merely a guide; its intricate lines formed a puzzle that promised to unlock the temple's hidden chambers, should they decipher it in time.
Jack traced the map's symbols with a fingertip, noting that the first challenge involved three massive glass slabs that needed to be angled toward the sun.
Emily, whose mind delighted in solving riddles, calculated the precise angles, recalling the position of the sun at that hour from the map's tiny sun-dial.
She whispered the numbers to Jack, who lifted the first slab, its surface catching the light and scattering prisms across the stone courtyard.
When the third glass settled into its final position, a resonant boom echoed through the square, and the massive stone doors shivered before grinding open.
Beyond the threshold, a vaulted hall unfolded, its walls adorned with frescoes that narrated the rise and fall of a civilization powered by the earth itself.
The paintings showed people harnessing luminous crystals, channeling their glow into sprawling conduits that fed the city's heart, a colossal stone pulsing with blue fire.
Emily sensed a growing instability; the stone's glow flickered, and the frescoes hinted at a looming collapse should the hidden code not be entered soon.
According to the map, a specific sequence of elemental symbols-water, fire, wind, earth-had to be pressed into a recessed console at the chamber's core.
Jack found the console, a circular slab of dark stone etched with the four sigils, each waiting for a careful touch.
Emily recalled a poem inscribed on a wall panel, its verses describing the order of the elements as a river flowing to the sea.
She whispered the first line, and together they pressed the water symbol, feeling a cool ripple travel through the stone, as if the city inhaled.
The fire sigil glowed crimson, and a warm gust brushed their faces, confirming that the second element had been accepted.
When they activated the wind, a soft sigh swept the hall, and the earth sigil pulsed, resonating with the deep blue stone at the center.
A moment of deafening silence followed, the kind that makes a heartbeat audible, as the city seemed to hold its breath.
Then the stone erupted in radiant light, the blue fire steadied, and the trembling walls ceased, as if the ancient power had been restored.
The city around them glowed anew; white walls shimmered with life, golden roofs caught the sun's last rays, and the gardens sang with color.
Emily felt a surge of triumph, yet a shadow of responsibility settled over her, for they had become custodians of a secret that could change the world.
Jack, still breathless, suggested they gather some of the strange books lying on stone shelves, eager to share their discovery with a specialist.
Emily hesitated, remembering the fragile balance that kept the city hidden, fearing that outside eyes might exploit the energy for selfish ends.
In a silent agreement, they left the volumes untouched, choosing instead to carry only the memory of the marvel and the promise to protect it.
As they turned to leave, the map on the stone table began to shimmer, its lines rearranging to reveal a new, smoother route back to the mountain path.
The newly drawn trail bypassed the treacherous gorge, winding gently through meadowland, promising a swift return before nightfall.
They walked slowly, savoring each detail-the delicate carvings on doorframes, the scent of jasmine in the gardens, the distant call of a lone hawk.
Emily glanced back once more, feeling the city's quiet gratitude settle like a warm ember in her chest.
They promised each other that, should the city ever call them again, they would answer, for the bond forged there was deeper than any ordinary adventure.
At the valley's edge, the sun sank low, painting the sky in scarlet and amber, while the distant mountains gathered shadows like looming giants.
When they finally reached their car, a thick veil of clouds rolled over the peak, concealing the hidden valley and erasing the city's silhouette from view.
Jack stared at the empty horizon, wondering if the city would still stand tomorrow or if it existed only for those daring enough to seek it.
Emily clutched the small stone box she had kept, its weight a quiet reminder of the secret they now shared, a promise etched in metal.
In the silence of the drive home, each contemplated the mystery of the ancient people, their hearts forever altered by the glimpse of a world beyond ordinary maps.

options: It highlights the city's abandonment, underscoring loss.
